LanguageData.RimJoust.IntroLetterText:
How to hold a jousting tournament:

1. Put a flag A and a flag B at each end of the lists, with a list barrier between them if you can.
2. Mount your colonists (Giddy-Up). They get a jousting lance automatically when the tournament starts.
3. Optional: assign some squires and place a recovery area and a dead spot. Squires drag the wounded and the dead off the lists for you.
4. Click a flag and pick "Hold tournament".

The winner becomes champion and crowns a Queen of Love and Beauty. Careful, a joust can kill.

For the details, the "Guide" button on a flag opens a full guide (also in the mod options).

LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.Title: Tournament guide
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.ListsBody:
A joust is run down the lists: a straight lane between two flags.

- Place a flag A and a flag B (Architect → Misc) at each end, on the same map. Use clearly different colors so you don't mix them up.
- A list barrier down the middle helps the horses charge straight.
- You can add a recovery area and a dead spot: squires use them to clear fallen knights.

Once the lists are laid out you never touch them again. Turning off "Show marker" on a flag hides it for clean screenshots without breaking anything.
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.RolesBody:
Select a colonist to see their role buttons.

Jouster: you pick who takes part in the tournament. If you mark no one, all your mounted colonists joust by default. Handy to enter only your best.

Squire: during a tournament they pick up fallen knights and carry them to the recovery area, clearing the lists between bouts. They need a recovery area placed so they know where to take them.
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.StartBody:
1. Mount your jousters (Giddy-Up). Any mount will do.
2. If you like, enter visitors from other factions as guest knights.
3. Click a flag and pick "Hold tournament".

The jousting lance is handed out automatically at the start and taken back at the end: nothing to craft. You need at least two ready jousters to start.
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.DuringBody:
Knights ride single elimination. On each pass a lance blow can unhorse the other rider: armor, shield, the jouster's skill (a mix of Melee for the strike and Animals for handling the mount) and traits all matter.

Open the tournament board to follow the current bout, the bracket and the journal. If a guest knight is in a bout, you can wager silver on it.

It stays dangerous: a blow can badly wound, or even kill.
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.AfterBody: The last one in the saddle is crowned champion. They then name a Queen of Love and Beauty and lay a crown of flowers in her lap.\n\nMost often they crown the one they love. But if they admire someone else far more, it can turn into a scandal, and the passed-over one will not forget. A window tells you who is crowned and why.
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.MeleeBody:
One rule: last one standing.

- Place the melee trophy post (Architect → Misc) in the middle of a clear ground, ideally fenced in with a door.
- Select the post: the white outline shows the arena boundary. The "Arena: auto" button fits it to your enclosure, the + and - buttons set a circle by hand. Fighters who leave are herded back to the center.
- Click "Start melee": colonists tagged as jousters dismount, get a blunted tourney mace (their own weapon comes back afterwards), form a circle, and at the horn everyone fights everyone.

Down means out, not dead: maces make bruises, not holes. The "Grand melee damage" slider in the options sets the brutality, and the crowd settles around the arena on its own.
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.ArcheryBody:
- Place the archery line flag, and the butt 10-20 cells across from it, with a clear lane between them. Nothing precious or alive behind the butt: stray arrows do not ask first.
- Click the flag: colonists tagged as jousters line up, each gets a loaner recurve bow (fairness first, we test the archer, not the arsenal), and shoot three volleys at the butt.

Every hit counts, with the shooter's name popping above the target. Most hits wins, Shooting skill breaks ties. Black eyes and bad arms cost accuracy, as they should. The crowd watches politely behind the line, never downrange.
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.GrandBody:
Three events back to back, like in the chronicles: the joust, the archery contest, then the grand melee.

- You need the full setup on the same map: the lists (flags A and B), the melee trophy post, the archery line and its butt.
- Mount your knights and click "Hold a GRAND tournament" on a lists flag. Mounted colonists compete, same as a regular tournament, and guest knights you entered stay for all three events.

Every event awards points by ranking. The wounded fight on as long as they can stand; anyone down skips the event. At the end, the total crowns the grand champion: a letter with the overall standings, honors, the Queen of Love and Beauty, and a "Grand tournament" entry in the hall of fame.
LanguageData.RimJoust.Guide.SafetyBody:
In the mod options you can set lance damage, unhorse chance, dangerous hit risk, fall damage, grand melee damage and the cooldown between tournaments.

Trait effects (brawler, tough, nimble, wimp, bloodlust, psychopath...) can be turned on or off.

Jousting uses no skill of its own: it leans on your Melee (the lance strike) and your Animals (handling the mount). The melee is pure Melee, and the archery contest pure Shooting. To make better champions, train all of it, at the quintain or in tournaments.
